c.tagline: Scandinavia's best-preserved medieval town, walled in roses and ruins.

taxi.fareNote: Uber and Bolt do not operate on Gotland; use local firms such as Taxi Gotland, booked by phone/app or from ranks by the harbour and airport. Confirm the 'jamforpris' (comparison price) shown on the window before you ride.

emergency.note: 112 reaches police, ambulance and fire anywhere in Sweden; 1177 is the non-emergency medical advice line.

hood_landmark.Innerstaden (Old Town): Visby old town cobblestone street ruins

avoid.reason: Late-night rowdiness and petty theft spike during the July party weeks (Almedalen and 'Stockholm week'), so watch bags in packed bars along the harbor.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed medieval heart inside the 3.4 km ring wall: cobbled lanes, church ruins, rose-covered stone cottages, cafes and the cathedral. Where almost every visitor wants to stay.
The waterfront by Almedalen park and the ferry harbour, home to the famous Almedalen political week, the marina, seafront restaurants and sunset views over the Baltic.
The coastal strip north of the walls with Norderstrand's long bathing beach, the Snäckgärdet resort area, campsites and swimming spots; relaxed and family-friendly in summer.

water.note: Tap water is safe and excellent throughout Sweden.

transit.hours: Town and island buses run roughly 6am to 8pm with reduced weekend service; there is no metro, tram or train on Gotland.
transit.pay: Visby's old town is compact and walkable; local and island buses (Kollektivtrafiken Gotland) are paid by app or contactless card, with single fares around SEK 30. Ferries to the mainland (Destination Gotland) are booked separately online. A car is largely unnecessary within the walls.

ferry: Visby Ferry Terminal (Destination Gotland to Nynäshamn & Oskarshamn)

tip.r: Not expected; service is included in the bill, though rounding up or leaving ~5-10% for good service is common.

landmarks: Visby City Wall (Ringmuren)
A remarkably intact 3.4-kilometre medieval ring wall with dozens of towers, encircling the UNESCO-listed Hanseatic town in 13th-century limestone.
Visby Cathedral (St. Mary's Church)
The only one of Visby's medieval churches still in use, consecrated in 1225, its distinctive black towers rising above the rooftops toward the sea.
St. Nicolai Church Ruin
The largest of Visby's dozen medieval church ruins, a Gothic Dominican priory whose roofless nave now hosts summer concerts under the open sky.
St. Karin (St. Catherine's) Church Ruin
A hauntingly beautiful Franciscan ruin on Stora Torget, its slender Gothic arcades framing the sky above the main square's café terraces.
Gotlands Museum (Fornsalen)
Gotland's treasure-packed museum displays Viking silver hoards, picture stones and grim relics of the 1361 Battle of Visby, including medieval mass graves.
Fiskargränd
Visby's most photographed lane, a narrow cobbled alley where climbing roses smother the walls of tiny tar-timbered fishermen's cottages each summer.
Kruttornet (The Powder Tower)
The oldest surviving building on the wall, a stout 12th-century harbour defence tower guarding what was once the Hanseatic port inlet.
Almedalen Park
A leafy park on the old Hanseatic harbour site, famous nationwide as the stage for Sweden's annual political festival, Almedalen Week.
DBW's Botanical Garden (Botaniska Trädgården)
A romantic 1855 garden inside the wall where roses, magnolias and exotic trees bloom around a church ruin, steps from the sea.
Kapitelhusgården
A medieval courtyard beside the cathedral ruins where stonemasons, glassblowers, and other craftspeople demonstrate traditional trades, especially lively during Medieval Week each August.

train.note: Gotland has had no railway since the island's narrow-gauge network closed in 1960, so there are no trains at all on the island, domestic or international. Rail travellers connect instead to the mainland ferry ports - Nynashamn is the end of a Stockholm commuter line, and Oskarshamn is served by SJ and regional trains (https://www.sj.se/en) - then cross by sea. The little train that trundles around Visby's old town is a sightseeing road vehicle, not a railway.

bus.note: No coach runs to Visby from abroad or from the Swedish mainland, because every road journey has to end at a ferry. On the island, Region Gotland's public bus network (Kollektivtrafiken Gotland, https://www.gotland.se/kollektivtrafik) radiates from the bus station at Osterport just outside the city wall to Farosund, Klintehamn, Ljugarn and the rest of Gotland, with sparse timetables outside the summer season. On the mainland, FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) and the regional transport authorities serve the ferry ports at Nynashamn and Oskarshamn, and Destination Gotland sells through bus-plus-ferry tickets from Stockholm.

ferry.note: Destination Gotland runs car-and-passenger ferries from Visby to Nynäshamn (near Stockholm, ~3 hr) and Oskarshamn (~3 hr) on the Swedish mainland, with several sailings daily in summer and fewer off-season. The terminal is in Visby harbour a few minutes' walk below the old town, so foot passengers need no onward transport. Hansa Destinations, a Rederi AB Gotland subsidiary, has also run a seasonal Rostock service calling at Visby and Nynashamn, but it sails at most weekly and the schedule changes from year to year, so confirm it before building a trip around it. Cars and campervans must be booked well ahead for July and August, when the island fills up.
